clue.text: People in general work like snobs to fill position

indicators.note: one set of letters is said to fill the word for position, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a place is a position
OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a work
U means upper-class, the label snobs give to their own usage

explanation.surface: A cynic sneers that ordinary folk behave like snobs to secure their station in life.
explanation.walkthrough: U-and-non-U was a 1950s British label for upper-class versus middle-class usage, so U stands for what snobs approve.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the common people of a country taken as a whole.

clue.text: Coming about ahead in shot on green thing with a noisy engine

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a putt is a golf stroke played on the green

indicators.note: coming about, like a ship turning, reads the word backwards

parts.note: up means ahead, as in a team being up by a goal

explanation.surface: A golfer leading the round putts while a noisy motor buzzes nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming about' is a sailing term for turning, so the letters run backwards; 'in' places them inside the golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-put is a small motorboat or motor named for its chugging sound.

clue.text: Support for The Scaffold's turn: origins of Lily the Pink boosted university visits

indicators.note: one piece visits the other, going inside it
in a down clue boosted means lifted upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn

indicators.note: the origins of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The Scaffold, a 1960s Liverpool group, had a hit with Lily the Pink; here their turn on a campus tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' takes LTP; 'boosted' turns GO+LTP into PTLOG; 'visits' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A putlog is a short horizontal pole whose end rests in brickwork, carrying scaffolding boards.

clue.text: Daily Record design officer initially lost such a plot?

parts.note: a log is a daily record, as a ship's log

indicators.note: lost says the letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: a logo is a design

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Scottish newspaper's design officer misplaced a story plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives O, and 'lost' drops it from LOGO. The Daily Record is a Scottish tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A log-log graph is plotted with logarithmic scales on both axes.

clue.text: Skilled tradespeople together broadcast '10 4!'

indicators.note: broadcast scatters, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, a metal container
4 written out as a word

explanation.surface: Workers in a craft send out radio code 10-4 as a sign of solidarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 points to the across answer; 'broadcast' rearranges its letters with FOUR. '10-4' is radio code for 'message received'.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft union organises skilled workers of one trade into one body.

clue.text: Colour in character in comic

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour; to tint is to colour

explanation.surface: An instruction to a cartoonist to add colour to a figure in a comic strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is wordplay, the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintin is the boy reporter hero of Hergé's Belgian comic-strip albums.

clue.text: Copied it stopping one getting married?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: mated means paired or married

explanation.surface: Was a forged document what kept a single person from marrying?
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce, so the past tense means copied.

clue.text: Starters from Tijuana a connoisseur of chilli's taken with it

definitions.text: Starters from Tijuana a connoisseur of chilli's taken with it

indicators.note: starters are the beginnings, the first letters of the next words

parts.note: hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A chilli lover in a Mexican border town samples appetisers.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is both wordplay and description: a crisp fried snack from Mexico eaten by a chilli fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco chip is a corn tortilla crisp, a Mexican-style appetiser.

clue.text: Perhaps access refused for this heir's failure to renew investiture

definitions.meaning: being refused access is a case of ..., not being let in
in feudal law ... is an heir's failure to renew investiture on succeeding

explanation.surface: A doorkeeper turns someone away because the heir did not renew a feudal title.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a Scots legal term from Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-entry is both being kept out and, in old Scots law, failing to take up a superior's grant.

clue.text: Podgorica once got over opening harangue, for the most part

indicators.note: one piece sits in the opening of the other, so it is placed inside
only most of the word is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a tirade is a long angry harangue

indicators.note: turned over, the word got is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone in the Montenegrin capital recovered after a rant began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns GOT round; 'for the most part' drops the last letter of the harangue, leaving TIRAD; 'opening' sets TOG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Montenegrin capital Podgorica bore the Yugoslav name Titograd, after Marshal Tito, from 1946 to 1992.

clue.text: Temperature of old Peruvian container

parts.note: an Incan is one of the Incas, the old rulers of Peru

explanation.surface: A museum label noting how hot an ancient Andean vessel was kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin can is a metal food container, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Before a judge, fabricating a truth pitilessly? Oh, no — not this!

definitions.text: Before a judge, fabricating a truth pitilessly? Oh, no — not this!

parts.note: to be up, or up before the beak, is to appear in court

indicators.note: fabricating means making up, so the letters are made into a new order
ruth is an old word for pity, so the word truth loses those letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness in court twists the truth mercilessly, and the cry goes up that this must not happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitilessly' strips RUTH from A TRUTH, leaving AT; 'fabricating' shuffles AT with OHNO into ONOATH. The whole clue describes perjury: lying is just what one must not do when sworn.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence given in court is sworn, and a witness lying in that state commits perjury.

clue.text: John might dance

parts.note: john and can are both American slang for a lavatory
might, as in being able to, is a sense of can

explanation.surface: A man named John is possibly going to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name but is a lavatory, a CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking Parisian music-hall routine, one kind of dance.

clue.text: Supporting De Niro cast with a set out in advance

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: cast means thrown, so the letters are flung into a new order

explanation.surface: A film actor backs Robert De Niro being cast in a role planned in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests film casting, but it rearranges DE NIRO A into EORDAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreordain is to predestine, decreeing something beforehand.

clue.text: Even less like an oil painting in Louvre with its frame retouched

definitions.text: Even less like an oil painting

indicators.note: a picture retouched is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the frame of Louvre is its outer letters, L and E

explanation.surface: A restorer's botched work on a Louvre canvas, frame and all, leaves it uglier still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its frame' means the outside letters of Louvre; 'retouched' rearranges them with IN LOUVRE. 'Not much of an oil painting' is a British idiom for plain-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is no oil painting means they are unattractive, so less lovely means even less of one.

clue.text: 0 x 1 — so gradually 5 became 12, 22 26, 1 down 3, or 19 21

parts.note: a binary digit, 0 or 1, is a bit
x is read 'by', as in 3 by 4
a binary digit, 0 or 1, is a bit

explanation.surface: A sum in binary, then a list showing how six-letter answers in the grid evolve.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest describes the theme: TINTIN turns into CANCAN via TINCAN, BOOBOO into TEETEE, and so on, one piece at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something bit by bit is doing it a little at a time, gradually.

clue.text: Tick nobody with droning voice

parts.note: a mo is a moment, as is a tick
not one means nobody

explanation.surface: Someone ticks off a person who talks in a dull drone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' is an informal British word for a moment, as in 'just a tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotone is a voice that stays on a single pitch, flat and droning.

clue.text: Austrian parts around which you've yet to go cycling

indicators.note: the parts go around inside the other letters, which surround them
cycling moves the end letter round to the front

parts.note: roles are parts in a play

explanation.surface: An Austrian region you have still to tour by bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go cycling' moves the last letter of yet to the front, giving TYE, which wraps around the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrolese describes the Tyrol, a mountain region of western Austria, or its people.

clue.text: Retreat from one who pulls big teeth?

parts.note: ivory is the tusks of elephants, the biggest teeth
a tower is one who tows, that is pulls

explanation.surface: Escaping the dentist who extracts large molars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulls' suggests extracting teeth, but it means towing: a TOWER here rhymes with 'mower'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is a sheltered place of withdrawal from practical realities, a retreat.

clue.text: Vulgar laugh that's emitted by brass section from below

indicators.note: in a down clue read from below means the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: wah-wah is the sound made by a muted trumpet or trombone

explanation.surface: A rude guffaw comes from the trumpets at the back of the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Haw-haw is a loud coarse laugh, and an affected upper-class one.

clue.text: Ship's parts stuck, to begin with, in a gateway to the Dales

indicators.note: in says one letter is placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Hawes is a market town in Wensleydale, a way into the Yorkshire Dales

indicators.note: to begin with picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boat jammed at the entrance to the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are an English national park of hill valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawses are the parts of a ship's bow through which the anchor cables run.

clue.text: Tolls finally followed by more of the same old taxes

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

parts.note: the same letter S again, several times: esses

explanation.surface: Road tolls, then yet more of the same levies of old.
explanation.walkthrough: After the S from 'Tolls', 'more of the same' asks for more S's: ESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sess is an archaic word for a tax or assessment, so sesses are old levies.

clue.text: Unnumbered British agent repeated blunder

indicators.note: repeated says the letters from the British agent are written out a second time
unnumbered strips away the number that follows the double zero

parts.note: the best-known agent is 007, James Bond, here read as OO SEVEN

explanation.surface: A British spy without a number keeps making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The agent is 007; unnumbered, the 7 goes and the two zeros stand as OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A boo-boo is a childish informal word for a silly mistake.

clue.text: Contraction of silver cracks beaker badly — result?

indicators.note: one piece cracks the other open and sits inside it
badly says the letters of beaker are put in disorder

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol, a shortened form, for silver

explanation.surface: Silver shrinking as it cools splits a laboratory beaker, and someone asks what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the vessel's letters to BREAKE and 'cracks' sets silver's symbol inside. The whole clue paints the scene that ends in a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakage is what you get when something cracks, the damage as outcome.

clue.text: One warming to Tootsie, this recipient of marching orders?

definitions.meaning: a knitted baby's shoe, warming the little feet or tootsies
Royal Marine slang for a recruit, one who is given orders to march

explanation.surface: Something cosy for a sweetheart, which then gets sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marching orders' suggests dismissal, but the second sense is a Royal Marines recruit, nicknamed after the bootneck.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies' woollen shoes warm the feet, and Marines slang names a trainee taking drill commands.

clue.text: Legendary spinner's general aches isolated in the heart

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the heart of these words, running across them

explanation.surface: A famous spin bowler's commander suffers pains centred in the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests cricket, but she spins the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Lachesis is the Fate who measures out the thread of each life, a mythical spinner.

clue.text: In the South American tropical forests you may find it dry

definitions.text: In the South American tropical forests you may find it
definitions.meaning: a ... or titi is a small South American monkey
dry means teetotal, and ... is slang for a teetotaller

explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' suggests the weather, which the rainforest is not; it means abstaining from drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives teetee as a spelling of titi, an Amazon monkey; and it is a short form for an abstainer.

clue.text: Opens Barking Women's Institute, reviving time one missed

indicators.note: barking means mad, so these letters are scrambled
reviving brings the words back in a new form, so their letters are rearranged
missed says these letters are left out of the larger mix

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dignitary opens a Women's Institute branch in Barking, east London, bringing back a forgotten moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite: the letters of WOMEN'S INSTITUTE, 'Barking' shuffled, minus those of TIME ONE ('reviving', 'missed'), give the answer. The Women's Institute is a British rural women's organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Untwisting a lid or a coiled rope undoes and so opens it.
